posts.cooked:
Mint. Three tips:

1) Cosmic Crest so Cosmic soaks the damage is much more use as a firsr play than the swords (although they make good plays on other people so Cos can keep the constructs healed up)

2) Drawn to the Flame really takes the sting out of having huge number of villain ongoings. “5 damage to everyone without killing myself? Don’t mind if I do.”

3) Dawn has back to back Auroras. Be aware and be prepared.

posts.name: Griff's Dad
posts.cooked:
Gah. Took me to my third time to win.

First time, I found myself with Citizens Truth, Anvil, and Hammer up. That's doom when you can't negate damage. I realized it was because the on-goings were too much. So second game, I went digging with K.N.Y.F.E.--used her power on herself looking for the Servo-Gauntlets. Never found them. You're going to get the RPG Launcher once, and that's it.

The first two games, I used the RPG Launcher to destroy Return with the Dawn. The third game, I took out Channel The Eclipse instead. That made a huge difference. I won with Ra incapped and everyone else in single digits because Dawn's cards came out a lot more slowly.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
First turn Cosmic Crest just means that Assault and Winter kill it before it helps much. That’s what I did, and what happened to me.

Tried once and lost once at this point. Dawn just has too many “play more stuff” ongoings, and the heroes only have a single RPG. I did make the mistake of shooting Return with the Dawn instead of Channel the Eclipse. In hindight, they’re both “play 1 extra card” ongoings, only Channel the Eclipse is worse because it can play more ongoings.

Not really sure what the optimal play with KNYFE is. I just used her on Ra, since Ra is always dealing damage.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Managed it the second time. Near mint.

Key differences:

Assault must die on turn 1 if Cosmic Crest is to live. Cosmic Crest ends up negating a ridiculous amount of damage if it sticks around, probably enough to turn the tide of the game by itself, considering that several heroes were near death at the end.

The RPG, when it shows up, must take out Channel the Eclipse. It’s much worse than Return with the Dawn.

Citizen Dawn will play Auroras back to back, since there’s nothing that reshuffles her draw deck. Which isn’t too bad, though the first one hurts.

Constructs are immune to Blazing Aurora, so KNYFE’s plays should all go to Captain Cosmic, helping him get stuff out. The constructs are, however, vulnerable to the area-effect minions (Winter, Hammer, Assault), so they’re high priority targets.

Wounding Buffer is a good way to zap AoE minions before they can hurt more than 1 target. Particularly if the Wounding Buffer is augmented by Imbued with Fire.

Dynamic Syphon on Ra is good once he has an AoE power, particularly Drawn to the Flame.

SMG and assault rifle are ways of pinging off Dynamic Syphon on Ra to get better AoE damage.

Citizen Hammer can one-shot constructs if Imbued Fire is out. Fortunately, Wounding Buffer took him out before he could smash all the constructs.

posts.name: FearLord
posts.cooked:
Mint. Slightly dicey turn where she flipped back and desastating Aura for the first time and her ongoings popped Assault and Winter back into play (while Battery was out) threatening to wipe my army of constructs out as well, but luckily Dynamic Syphon and Conduit Blade allowed Ra to take out Winter before she could do anything.

With a lot of my set up gone, it took a little longer to finish her, but it was manageable and enough people had Swords from Captain Cosmic that I could keep some damage on until she went down. Everyone in the teens apart from Ra who was lower due to using his base power a few times (and having a Wounding Buffer that meant he hit himself twice...)

Quite satisfying absorbing damage from Dawn and Battery though...
